minimum_requirements: source or demonstrated evidence is verifiable enough to state the claim honestly
meaningfully relevant or transferable to 3D/game-art production, animation, technical art, DCC/engine workflows, AI production, or visual-development reference
contains at least one concrete production, technical, workflow, testing, animation-reference or visual-development takeaway
admit_as_brief_examples: useful tutorial with one transferable technique
verified DCC add-on or small workflow tool with a concrete use case
shader or technical-art demonstration with a reproducible idea
animation showcase with strong pose, timing, arc, weight or visual-reference value
character or environment visual-development reference with a concrete production takeaway
credible community or Reddit experience when claims are scoped to what the source actually demonstrates
single-source official or creator-authored announcement with a concrete capability but limited independent evidence
substantive_delta_examples: new quality result or production test
new benchmark or measurable performance result
new limitation, failure mode or compatibility finding
new API, export, licensing, pricing or availability change with production consequence
new use case that materially changes how the known tool can be applied
hard_exclude_only: marketing or generic hype with no concrete demonstrated capability or takeaway
unrelated to game art and not meaningfully transferable
previously published canonical identity without any substantive delta
no identifiable production, technical, workflow, testing, animation-reference or visual-development takeaway

window_policy.24h: Prioritize fresh releases, changelogs, model/tool updates and meaningful production news. Fresh valid intelligence always gets first claim on the five category slots.
window_policy.7d: Backfill strong unpublished production workflows, breakdowns, tests, add-ons, DCC/engine techniques and AI-assisted production findings when fresh items do not fill the category target.
window_policy.30d: Backfill strong production cases, workflow breakdowns, technical-art examples and credible community/GitHub discoveries that remain operationally useful and were not previously published.
window_policy.6m: Backfill high-value research, technical references, conference material, official documentation and missed production intelligence that is still relevant and absent from the Published Intelligence Registry.
window_policy.evergreen: Final fill tier only: use verifiable, still-current official documentation, production workflow references or case studies with concrete operational value. Evergreen items must be unpublished and must never be low-value filler.

collection.fill_target_policy: Continue discovery through the configured fill ladder aiming for 30 total valid unpublished items after Published Intelligence Registry dedupe and the admission gate. Twenty items is the normal release floor, not a discovery stop signal. After admission passes, limited evidence depth must route to BRIEF rather than rejection. Narrower-impact items may be downranked instead of discarded. Category counts are diversity diagnostics, not release quotas. Never pad with duplicates, unverifiable claims or items with no concrete production/reference takeaway.

A.label: major-intelligence
A.guidance: New models, major versions, meaningful feature/workflow changes, pricing/licensing/availability changes, or major engine/DCC/AI production developments. Strong TOP5 candidates when production impact is high.

B.label: production-intelligence
B.guidance: Practical character/prop/environment workflows, modeling, retopology, UV, texturing, material/shader, rigging, animation, mocap, cleanup, retarget, Unity/Unreal production techniques, AI 3D or AI motion tests, pipeline/tooling improvements and measurable production lessons. These are valid intelligence even without a major product announcement.

C.label: case-tip-community
C.guidance: Credible cases, tutorials, tips, Blender/DCC add-ons, GitHub tools, shader/technical demonstrations, research prototypes, community experiences, animation references and visual-development showcases are admissible when the source is verifiable and at least one concrete production or reference takeaway can be stated. Limited depth should normally become BRIEF; narrower impact lowers ranking rather than causing rejection.

exclude: marketing or generic hype with no concrete demonstrated capability or takeaway
items unrelated to 3D/game-art production and not meaningfully transferable
previously published canonical identity without a substantive delta
content with no identifiable production, technical, workflow, testing, animation-reference or visual-development takeaway
collection.completeness_trigger_policy: Release-ready when 20-30 valid unpublished items survive Published Intelligence Registry dedupe and the admission gate after the configured discovery ladder has been reasonably exhausted. Target and maximum are 30. Limited evidence depth is handled by BRIEF classification rather than admission rejection. Category shortages do not block release and must never be padded.
collection.ranking_guidance: Admission is intentionally broader than ranking. Production value, practical applicability, source verifiability, user-interest fit and freshness drive rank after admission. Narrow impact, older age or limited evidence may lower rank but should not by themselves reject a verified item with one concrete production/reference takeaway. Aim for broad six-category coverage without enforcing equal quotas and continue discovery toward 30 even after reaching the 20-item release floor.

production_intelligence_profile.purpose: Surface intelligence most likely to improve game-art production quality, efficiency, pipeline decisions, testing priorities or workflows over the next 6-24 months.
production_intelligence_profile.category_quota_policy: Interest scores and preferences guide discovery/ranking only; never create per-category quotas or filler.

ranking.freshness_rule: Prefer newer when production value is comparable; allow 1-6 month or evergreen material to outrank fresh low-value news.
ranking.source_rule: Official, community, video, case, GitHub and research sources are all admissible when verifiable; source type alone does not determine rank.
ranking.selection_rule: Use a mixed slate: consequential updates first, then the strongest tests, workflows, breakdowns, tools, references and cases. After the broad admission gate, lower production impact or limited evidence depth lowers ranking or routes to BRIEF instead of causing automatic rejection. Category and tool preferences are ranking/discovery signals, not quotas.

global_positive_signals: NPR, toon or stylized technical value
clear risk, limitation or failure analysis
global_downrank: showcase with little production detail unless its category explicitly permits strong reference value
old content used mainly to fill quantity
global_hard_exclude: published identity or normalized source without substantive delta
unrelated to game art and not meaningfully transferable
generic hype or marketing with no concrete demonstrated capability or takeaway
no identifiable production, technical, workflow, testing, animation-reference or visual-development takeaway

tool_tiers.emerging: Other new tools qualify when they show a meaningful breakthrough.

ai2d_downrank: Photoshop or DCC integration without meaningful workflow gain
ai-generation.ai_motion_video_rule: Video-only character motion may qualify without skeletal export when it provides concrete animation reference, previs or production value.
downrank: repeat introduction of a known tool without delta
ai-generation.backfill: Actively allow unpublished 1-6 month and evergreen production tests or workflows when they provide strong production value.

3d-production.prop_policy: Hard-surface assets, weapons, mechanical assets, vehicles and game props are high priority.
3d-production.style_policy: Stylized, NPR, semi-realistic and realistic or AAA all score 5; style is not an admission gate.
3d-production.tutorial_policy: Useful tutorials qualify when they provide at least one concrete transferable production technique; novelty, major-news status or FULL-level evidence depth may improve ranking but are not admission requirements.
3d-production.breakdown_policy: Industry production breakdowns are high priority.
hard_exclude: pure portfolio or showcase with no identifiable production method, technical takeaway or usable visual-development/reference value
beginner content with no transferable production takeaway
breakdown that provides neither an actual method nor a concrete production/reference takeaway
3d-production.backfill: Older strong production cases qualify but rank below equally valuable recent material.

3d-animation.gameplay_cinematic: Gameplay and cinematic animation have equal baseline priority; production value decides rank.
3d-animation.breakdown_policy: High-quality animation breakdowns are high priority even when they are not news.
3d-animation.showcase_policy: Pure animation showcase may qualify when animation quality or reference value is strong enough despite limited workflow detail.
3d-animation.tool_policy: Actively discover rig, retarget, pose, motion-editing, mocap-cleanup and procedural-animation production tools.

unreal_priorities: new version features with art-production impact
hard_exclude: pure programming or engineering content with no material art-production relevance

emerging-case.research_policy: Novel research may enter when it is verifiable and exposes at least one concrete production-relevant capability, limitation or transferable idea; near-usability increases ranking but is not an admission gate.
emerging-case.open_source_policy: Research code or GitHub projects qualify when they provide a concrete demonstrated capability or production-relevant takeaway, even if maturity is limited; immaturity should route to BRIEF and lower ranking.
emerging-case.gaussian_nerf: Normal priority; boost when Gaussian Splatting, NeRF or novel-view work becomes materially productionized.
emerging-case.world_model: Include when there is credible game or 3D-production potential.
emerging-case.4d: Include dynamic 3D or 4D research when it has credible production potential.
emerging-case.conference_policy: Allow GDC, SIGGRAPH, Unreal Fest, GTC, Unity and similar conference backfill; newer material wins when production value is equal.
emerging-case.failure_case_policy: Failure cases qualify only when they explain causes, cost, quality limits or pipeline consequences.
hard_exclude: pure mathematical derivation without production consequence

blender-dcc.blender_tip_policy: Useful small Blender tips qualify when they save time, improve quality or simplify workflow.
blender-dcc.maya_policy: Include Maya content when its production method has meaningful cross-DCC transferable value.
blender-dcc.houdini_policy: All major Houdini production areas are discoverable; rank by production value rather than enforcing a Houdini quota.
blender-dcc.new_tool_policy: Include niche or new DCC tools when they provide a concrete production workflow, time-saving use case or transferable technique; narrow impact lowers ranking instead of blocking admission.
hard_exclude: DCC use unrelated to game art and not meaningfully transferable

full_analysis.quality_rule: Each block must add one distinct, source-supported production insight; do not pad to a character quota or restate summary/quick_impact.
writing_guidance: All Full Analysis block headings must be concise Traditional Chinese. Keep necessary product names, DCC/engine names, abbreviations and technical terms such as UE5, UV, AI, Meshy or Blender when they improve precision, but do not use English-only or English-dominant headings.
Use concise content-specific Traditional Chinese headings such as 動作製作流程、Rig / Retarget 流程、貼圖工作流、遊戲資產流程、製作價值、導入測試 or 實測 instead of fixed report-template headings.
Choose 3 to 5 analysis angles according to the item itself. Do not force every item into the same four headings.
Prefer fast-scanning production notes: state the concrete capability or delta, explain the practical workflow value, then give an adoption/test/risk judgment when relevant.
Keep V3 information depth, but avoid verbosity, filler, repeated context, and minimum-character padding.

For AI motion/animation, when supported by the source, prioritize input, output/rig compatibility, root motion/fingers/face/multi-person, cleanup/foot lock, retarget, local/cloud, speed, licensing and engine integration.
The 2026-09-01 Full Analysis tone and structure is the readability reference; do not rewrite historical pages to the new schema.

collection_guidance: Prioritize practical game-art asset creation rather than treating individual technical steps as standalone intelligence categories.
character-production covers character modeling, sculpting, hair, cloth, character textures/materials and end-to-end character workflows.
prop-production covers props, weapons, hard-surface assets, prop textures/materials and production techniques.
environment-production covers environment art, architecture, vegetation, terrain, modular environments, environment materials and asset workflows.

production-workflow covers cross-asset methods such as modeling, retopology, UV, baking, texturing, materials, scanning, procedural production, pipeline and efficiency tools when they are not specific to one asset type.
When an item is clearly about a character, prop or environment workflow, classify it by that asset type even if the technique itself is UV, texturing, materials or retopology.
